title: Platform systems & services: playbook, runbooks, dashboards, alerts and roadmap (2026-Q4)
author: Asha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook consolidates platform engineering guidance for systems and services operated by the Platform team: runbooks, standard how-tos, dashboard and alerting conventions, retrospective format, and the near-term roadmap. It is intended as the single source of truth for on-call engineers, new hires, and partnering teams (SRE, infra, product).

Scope
- Services: platform-api, infra-controller, telemetry-collector, autoscaler, deployment-coordinator
- Environments: prod, staging, integration (non-customer)
- Topics: operational runbooks, dashboards & alerts, escalation, retrospectives, roadmap & ownership

Contents
1) Systems & services overview
2) How-tos (deploys, feature flags, scaling actions)
3) Dashboards and alerting conventions
4) Runbooks (incident playbooks)
5) Retrospective template and triage process
6) Roadmap (2026-Q4 through 2027 roadmap seeds)

---

1) Systems & services overview

Short descriptions (owners and SLAs)
| Service | Responsible Team | Primary Function | SLA (prod) | Owner |
| platform-api | Platform | API gateway / orchestration for internal platform features | 99.95% availability; p95 < 150ms | @platform-backend |
| infra-controller | Platform | Orchestrates infra provisioning & reconciles desired state | 99.9% availability; p95 < 500ms | @platform-infra |
| telemetry-collector | Observability | Ingests metrics/traces/alerts from nodes | 99.9% availability; ingestion lag < 10s | @observability |
| autoscaler | Platform | Scaling decisions for dedicated pools | 99.9% availability; scale action within 30s typical | @platform-scaling |
| deployment-coordinator | Platform | Coordinated canary & rollout engine | 99.9% availability; rollout latency measured in minutes | @platform-release |

Service boundaries and contracts
- All services expose a /healthz and /ready endpoint; readiness gating is used by deployment-Coordinator.
- Standard request/response formats are JSON with schema versioning header: X-Platform-Schema: v1.
- Backwards-compat compatibility: major schema changes must be announced in the platform-team slack channel and have a deprecation window of >= 30 days.

Ownership & contacts
- On-call rotation: platform on-call (primary) -> infra on-call (secondary) -> observability (pager for telemetry incidents). See the team wiki for rotation schedule.

---

2) How-tos (select common operations)

A. Deploying a service (recommended flow)
1. Create a PR with a clear description and CHANGELOG entry.
2. CI will run unit tests, integration tests, and a smoke deploy to staging.
3. Run the canary deploy via deployment-coordinator: select 5% traffic for 15m.
4. Verify key metrics: error_rate < 0.1% above baseline, p95 latency within 10% of baseline.
5. Promote to 50% then 100% if metrics stable.

CLI example
- Trigger canary (local):
```
$ platformctl rollout --service platform-api --canary 5 --duration 15m
```

B. Emergency rollback (fast path)
1. From the dashboard, identify the rollback button for the current active release.
2. If the button is not available, open the deployment-coordinator console and run:
```
$ platformctl rollback --service platform-api --to-last-stable
```
3. Notify #platform-incident channel with summary and affected regions.
4. Open a postmortem in the platform retrospective template (link below).

C. Adding a dashboard panel
- Use Grafana dashboard templates stored in git: infra/observability/dashboards.
- New panels must include: metric name, query, baseline explanation, and owners field. Submit as PR to dashboards repo.

---

3) Dashboards and alerting conventions

General rules
- Dashboards live in the dashboards repo and are provisioned via the grafana-operator. Do not create ad-hoc dashboards in the UI for critical alerts.
- Naming convention: team-service-metric e.g., platform-platform-api-latency.
- All dashboards must list the owner(s) in the top-right panel and link to the runbook.

SLOs and alert thresholds (examples)
- platform-api availability SLO: 99.95% monthly. Alert: page when availability drops below 99.9% for 10m.
- platform-api p95 latency: SLO p95 < 150ms. Alert: page when p95 > 300ms for 5m.
- telemetry-collector ingestion lag: SLO < 10s. Alert: warn when lag > 15s for 3m; page when lag > 30s for 5m.
- autoscaler failed scale actions: page when >5 failures in 10m.

Alert routing & severity
- Sev2 (page): service unavailable (>=10% traffic impacted), major error rate spike (>1% sustained 5m), or critical data loss.
- Sev3 (notify): localized errors affecting a subset of customers, single region degradation.
- Pager duty escalation: 15 minutes to acknowledge; 30 minutes to escalate to secondary if unresolved.

Alert runbook link mapping (example)
- Alert name: platform-api-high-p95 -> runbook: platform-api/high-p95-runbook

---

4) Runbooks (incidents)

Runbook: platform-api high latency (p95)
Severity: Sev2 -> page
Owner: platform-backend on-call
Steps:
1. Confirm alert: check Grafana panel and query the last 30 minutes.
   - Query example (PromQL):
     sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"platform-api\"}[5m])) by (le)
2. Check downstream dependencies: telemetry-collector, infra-controller, database (platform-config-store).
3. If downstream is healthy, capture a flame graph (profiling service) and inspect recent deploys.
4. If caused by a recent deploy, roll back to last stable. See Emergency rollback above.
5. If caused by traffic surge, consider immediate scale up of dedicated pools:
```
$ platformctl scale --pool platform-dedicated --replicas +2
```
6. Notify stakeholders and create incident in the incident tracker: platform-incidents. Include: timeline, affected regions, mitigation steps.
7. Close the incident once metrics return to baseline for 30 minutes; start postmortem within 48 hours.

Runbook: node OOM (infra-controller)
Severity: Sev2
1. Identify the node and check kubelet logs.
2. Cordon the node and drain workloads: `kubectl cordon <node>` then `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets`
3. If OOM is reproducible, increase memory limit for offending pods or adjust vertical autoscaler target.
4. Replace the node if hardware fault suspected: follow cloud provider-specific workflow (see onprem-packaging playbook for on-prem replacement).

Post-incident checklist
- Ensure mitigation has stopped customer impact.
- Create a timeline with <5 minute granularity.
- Determine root cause and contributing factors.
- Assign action items and owners; target implementation dates.
- Runbook updates: update the runbook to include new steps learned.

---

5) Retrospectives and triage process

Retrospective template (use for any Sev2+ incident)
- Summary (1-2 sentences)
- Timeline (what happened and when)
- Root cause analysis (RCA)
- Contributing factors (people, process, tech)
- What went well
- Action items (owner, due date, verification criteria)
- Follow up (monitoring or verification plan)

Triage cadence
- Postmortem draft due: 72 hours after incident.
- Postmortem review meeting: within 7 days with 30–60 minute time-box.
- High-severity action items must be added to the platform roadmap with a priority tag.

---

6) Roadmap (near-term priorities and ownership)

Q4 2026 priorities (Owner tags and ETA)
- Observability migration to TraceX (Elena Gomez) — ETA: 2026-11-30 — Deliverables: reduced trace ingestion cost by 25%, unified span sampling policy.
- Standardized dashboard templates & autosync (Marcus Li) — ETA: 2026-12-15 — Deliverables: dashboard repo CI + grafana provisioning.
- Runbook automation (Asha Patel) — ETA: 2026-12-31 — Deliverables: API to trigger rollbacks, standardized runbook URL metadata in alerts.
- Improved autoscaler decision logic (Priya Nair) — ETA: 2027-01-31 — Deliverables: smarter scale-down policy to reduce thrash and lower cost by 8%.

Backlog seeds (2027)
- Private deployment runbook harmonization with onprem packaging team.
- Cost-visible dashboards per customer for Dedicated customers.
- Canary analysis improvements (automated statistical checks).

Roadmap process and how to propose changes
- Raise roadmap items as a PR to the platform-roadmap repo with: problem statement, success metrics, rough effort and owner.
- Roadmap grooming occurs bi-weekly during platform planning. Major scope changes require product review.
